image_description: A high-angle shot of a bathroom scene featuring a white toilet with the lid up. On the toilet seat, there is a large, chaotic pile of empty cardboard toilet paper tubes (cores). To the left, on the floor next to a small trash can or holder, sits a single full roll of toilet paper. The lighting is dim and warm, casting shadows.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dominant subject on the toilet is a pile of *empty* cardboard cores, not rolls wound with paper. Only one actual roll is visible on the floor.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Roll is compact with modest diameter and width, suitable for standard bathroom holder.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The single roll on the floor appears to have standard dimensions.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Resolution is too low to verify perforation details on the single roll; the pile of cores has no sheets.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Cannot resolve surface texture due to image blur and distance.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Cardboard core visible at center of roll.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The core is clearly visible in the single roll on the floor, and the pile on the toilet consists entirely of these cores.
The objects are white/off-white, consistent with the class.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Image resolution prevents verification of fibrous texture.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Household paper product in roll format.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The items are clearly household toilet paper products.

artifact_observations.location: Pile of tubes on toilet seat
artifact_observations.reasoning: The pile of cardboard tubes exhibits physically improbable stacking and fusion. Several tubes appear to melt into one another or float without clear support points, defying gravity and rigid body physics.
The interior of the toilet bowl lacks clear definition and water reflection, appearing as a smooth, muddy gradient rather than distinct ceramic and water surfaces.
The lines of the floor tiles and wall panels show slight warping and inconsistency in vanishing points, suggesting weak geometric grounding.

To analyze the depth relationships in the chaotic pile and detect any foreground-background bleeding or impossible overlaps.
To check for fusion artifacts where individual tubes merge into each other, violating topological boundaries.
To assess general image coherence, lighting consistency, and noise levels.

Boundary separation between individual tubes in the pile
